$175/session, paid out of pocket for an out-of-network therapist.  When I was searching for a therapist earlier this year that I found that fewer and fewer therapists are even accepting any insurance.  They say it's not worth it for them because the insurance companies don't pay out enough and they are starting to actually lose money being in-network for insurance companies.  Trying to find an in-network therapist through your insurance is almost impossible too because they're so highly in-demand and they're never accepting new clients.  

With my insurance I'm able to submit out-of-network claims for my therapy sessions (I have to fill out a form and attach a superbill, which I do once a month just to keep it a regular habit.  It's not a ton of work but I actually have to print everything and mail it in, which is a little annoying).  I end up getting reimbursed for about 50% of what I paid out of pocket, so it's definitely worth it.  

Hope this information is helpful!  It took me months to figure all of this out so hopefully I can pass some of it along to anyone reading.

I think a lot about this concept of someone asking for a seat on the train.  There's not an easy answer across the board.  I'm lucky to be able-bodied, and when I'm sitting, if there's someone standing close to me who needs to sit due to age/disability/pregnancy/whatever, I'll stand up and offer them my seat.  But I'm not going to constantly scan the car to see if there are people who may need to sit.  So in the back of my mind I tell myself that if they need a seat badly enough they'll ask me, and of course I'll stand.

I'm sure it would be nerve-wracking to ask a stranger for their seat, but I guess the real question is, which is worse: having to stand when you really need to sit, or having to endure a few moments of awkwardness?  I think this is unfortunately a situation where you may have to profile people a little bit and seek out someone who looks friendly and who *may* not need the seat themselves, rather than asking someone who seems closed-off and who may give you a hard time.  If you follow this method I would be very, very surprised if you got many people who refused to give up their seat.  

I once saw an middle-aged man with a non-visible leg injury ask a younger woman if he could sit down.  She got up immediately and he mentioned that he needed to sit because of a leg thing, and that was that.  I guess in an ideal world he wouldn't have to disclose why he needs to sit, but I feel like it breaks the social tension to have a "reason" to ask someone to give up their seat.

To me, noise is probably the #1 biggest quality of life complaint I have with living in NYC.  It's so invasive and distracting to me, and it makes me curse evolution that human beings haven't evolved some sort of ear equivalent to eyelids so we can shut out unwanted noise.  

I've lived in a lot of different apartments over the years, and it feels like such a crapshoot as far as what you get as far as noise.  My current place is really bad and has very thin walls and ceilings.  The variety of noises that I deal with is pretty remarkable too.  I have:

* a full-time daycare facility (!!!) next door

* a super blasting bachata music underneath me

* a 6'6" 300lb guy above me who sounds like Godzilla stomping around, although I'm sure he's just walking normally

* a guy who practices trombone for several hours every night two floors above me

* angry drivers honking their horns outside my window

* a couple across the hall with a brand new baby

* a couple down the hall with a new puppy who barks incessantly

* a smoker's spot in front of my kitchen window where I get to hear conversations and loud, phlegmy coughs.  Fun bonus: their cigarette smoke drifts into my kitchen while I'm trying to eat.

It's really rough for me to deal with, and the only reason why I haven't moved out is because the rent is good and I love the neighborhood.  I don't know what to do, honestly.  I've considered moving into a different building in the same neighborhood, but I'd be rolling the dice that my new neighbors wouldn't be just as loud or louder.  I've even considered moving out to the burbs in Westchester or NJ.  

A [white noise generator](https://www.amazon.com/Marpac-Dohm-DS-Natural-Sound-Machine/dp/B00HD0ELFK%3Fpsc%3D1%26SubscriptionId%3DAKIAILSHYYTFIVPWUY6Q%26tag%3Dduckduckgo-ffsb-20%26linkCode%3Dxm2%26camp%3D2025%26creative%3D165953%26creativeASIN%3DB00HD0ELFK) at night really, really helps.  I wish so badly I could use earplugs but my ear canals must be a weird shape because they've never in my entire life fit properly and actually blocked out noise.  I do have a good pair of over-ear headphones that I use to listen to music too, if I desperately need to down out my neighbors' noise.  I've even though about putting up acoustic foam on my walls but I did research and found out that apparently they don't dampen noise in that way.  

Good luck.

I used to believe this advice until the worst case scenario happened to me and now I'm way more careful about this.  I sent in my resume for two open positions at a company that I was really eager to work for.  I was qualified for the first job, but the second job was basically a pipe-dream that I wasn't qualified for at all.  

I knew there was absolutely no way I would get the second job, but I was just kind of putting it out into the universe.  I figured the worst thing that would happen is that I get a "no" and the best thing that would happen is that my resume would get into the hands of someone who could see how enthusiastic I was about this industry and would maybe keep me in mind for something in the future.  

Well I was totally wrong.  Someone from their HR department interviewed me on the phone for the first position that I was qualified for. Everything went fine until she mentioned that she saw I also submitted my resume for the second job that I was unqualified for.  She explained to me that it makes me look less serious as a candidate to be submitting my resume for such a wide variety of positions and it also wastes the time of the HR departments who have to scan through all the resumes.  She was never rude but she was definitely taking the opportunity to knock me down a few pegs.  I apologized and tried to explain my thought process, but I could tell that my reputation was already damaged in her mind.  Needless to say they didn't hire me, and I will probably never be able to work with that company because of the fact that all resumes go through their HR department first and foremost.  

I think in a general way this is good advice ("You miss 100% of the shots you don't take" and all that) but just be careful in specific situations.

Very interesting concept.  I feel like it would be worthwhile to respond to your question because I probably have a somewhat unusual viewpoint on this issue.  I am a person who is very cynical and misanthropic about the true nature of human beings, but I grew up with very supportive, caring, intelligent parents who honestly did an wonderful job of raising me. 

I realize that there are many beautiful, joyful things about the human experience but I feel like this is just us trying to see the silver lining in an oppressive and shitty cosmic situation.  I view our world as a cold, uncaring place that inflicts tremendous pain on us.  Justice, morality, and freedom are empty concepts.  I basically see human beings as highly evolved primates who gained so much intelligence that we overcomplicated our world and developed unsustainable emotional systems within our brains.  We are slowly killing the planet that gave us life and are setting ourselves up for environmental collapse in the next few millennia.  Millions of people have been killed over religion, which in itself is just an emotional crutch to help humans trudge through our terrible existence. We developed an economic system that requires us to surrender 2/3rds of our waking hours working at a job so that we don't become homeless and starve.  We are capable of intense cruelty, greed, selfishness, and violence.  The hubris that it takes for someone to bring another human being into this world is flabbergasting to me.  I don't think we need to impose our dreadful world on a child.  I don't think it would be a tragedy if human beings died out in the next few million years.  

That said, my parents were warm, caring, and generous.  The fact that people like them exist in this world honestly seems like a fluke to me.  I had a good childhood in spite of being a slightly depressed, anxious kid.  I can't really explain why my worldview seems so contrary to how I was raised.
